name: FSW World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Five Star Wrestling's top championship, in both of its runs. Steve Johnson won it first, beating Matthew Morrison in the final of a tournament at High Impact on 27 August 2000. It changed hands often over the next year and was stripped from its champion more than once; Chris Fear won it at Hallowed Knights on 7 October 2001, and Blitz pinned Fear for it at Futile Resistance in November 2001. When the fed returned in 2002 the title was vacant: a four-way for it at Genesis on 18 August 2002 was ruled a no contest, and Timo Bolamba won it at Bad Moon Rising on 20 October 2002, pinning Mike Marvelous in the final of the Dead or Alive tournament. Bolamba beat Chris Chase in his first defence on 27 November 2002, the last show the surviving record holds.
notes: Sources: the fed's own title history on thefsw.com, as the Wayback Machine captured it on 8 April and 31 October 2001; its 2002 Title Histories page; the show write-ups of both runs; the August 2000 tournament bracket. The 2002 write-ups bill Bolamba's belt as new and call its first holder the first FSW World Champion, while the 2002 Title Histories page numbers his reign sixteenth, after those of 2000–01, and Bad Moon Rising bills Mike Marvelous a former World Heavyweight Champion. The October 2001 page dates Johnny Mayhem's first win "4/17/02"; its own order, its Intercontinental row and the April 2001 calendar put that Glory on 17 April 2001. The 2002 page dates Bad Moon Rising 21 October 2002; the show and its advertisements give Sunday 20 October.

name: FSW Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: A championship of the fed's first run. Cyle Chaos became the first FSW Intercontinental Champion by climbing a ladder for the belt at High Impact on 27 August 2000. Big Daveylicious, Mike Marvelous, Colin Baird, Jacob Jackson, Aggonizer and Johnny Mayhem were among its holders before Painkiller, the boss, made Mayhem lay the belt down on 6 April 2001. Punisher 2000 won it at Hallowed Knights on 7 October 2001, and Jonny Trip pulled it down in a ladder match at Futile Resistance in November 2001; the fed's champions page still listed Trip at the end of that year. The 2002 run did not bring the title back.
notes: Sources: the fed's own title history on thefsw.com, as the Wayback Machine captured it on 8 April and 31 October 2001; the first run's show write-ups; the Futile Resistance preview card ("Punisher 2000(c)"); the champions page captured on 28 December 2001. The October 2001 page names Carlton Carter beaten on 15 May 2001, where its previous row makes neXt the champion.

name: FSW Rising Star Championship
epitaph: A championship of the fed's first run. Its first champion was crowned at High Impact on 27 August 2000: The Riddler in the show's own write-up, Aggonizer in the fed's title history. Red Hurricane won it at Total Annihellation that October, Colin Baird took it in a Hell In A Cell ladder match at Fallen, and neXt, champion from March 2001, handed the belt to Max Danger on 10 April 2001, saying he was moving on to higher things. Jack Brooze won it at Hallowed Knights on 7 October 2001, and PS Mad pinned him for it and the Extreme title together at Futile Resistance in November 2001.
notes: Sources: the fed's own title history on thefsw.com, as the Wayback Machine captured it on 8 April and 31 October 2001; the first run's show write-ups; the Futile Resistance preview card ("Jack Brooze(c)"). The High Impact and Total Annihellation write-ups have The Riddler win the title and lose it to Red Hurricane; both captures of the title history give those two lines to Aggonizer. The 15 July 2001 row names the card Paranoia; the same page's other rows of that date, and the fed's booking, say Defiance.

name: FSW Extreme Championship
epitaph: The first run's hardcore championship. Mike Marvelous, refereeing, awarded it to Jacob Jackson at High Impact on 27 August 2000 when time ran out, though Dysan believed he had won. Jack Miller held it three times; at Final Destination on 26 November 2000 he ran Hardcore Camo over with a car in the parking lot and took the belt on the same night Camo had won it. Jack Brooze won it vacant at Redemption on 26 August 2001. A Paranoia write-up of October 2001 has P.S. Mad pin Brooze for it; at Futile Resistance in November 2001 Brooze is billed champion again and PS Mad wins it from him, together with the Rising Star title, and the fed's champions page still listed him at the end of the year.
notes: Sources: the fed's own title history on thefsw.com, as the Wayback Machine captured it on 8 April and 31 October 2001; the first run's show write-ups, among them an undated Paranoia results page of October 2001; the Futile Resistance preview card ("Jack Brooze(c)"); the champions page captured on 28 December 2001. The October 2001 title history ends with Jack Brooze and carries no line for the Paranoia change.

name: FSW Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Five Star Wrestling's tag team championship, in both of its runs. The Psycho Brotherz won it first in a four-corner elimination match at High Impact on 27 August 2000. It was stripped or vacated more than once in the first run, and P.S. Mad and Sound, who won it at Love Hurts on 26 February 2001, declared the belts the Hardcore Tag Titles. At Futile Resistance in November 2001 Human took the title from Blake in a parking lot and then held it alone. In 2002 Ming and Michel Krieg won it vacant at Genesis on 18 August, Bad Frotitude took it in a three-way on 26 September, and at Bad Moon Rising on 20 October the masked Dead Presidents won it from Bad Frotitude in a chain match and unmasked as Politically Incorrect, William S. Powell and Reginald V. Lovecraft. Rites To Pain, Jason McAllister and Neurosis, won it from them on 27 November 2002, the last show the surviving record holds.
notes: Sources: the fed's own title history on thefsw.com, as the Wayback Machine captured it on 8 April and 31 October 2001; its 2002 Title Histories page; the show write-ups of both runs; the champions page captured on 28 December 2001. The 2002 page has Ming and Michel Krieg beat Bad Frotitude at Genesis, where the write-up has them beat A Tag Team; it dates the Jacksons' title 29 November 2000 (Fallen, 29 October, on its own World list) and Bad Moon Rising 21 October 2002.

name: FSW Prime Time Championship
epitaph: Mike Marvelous became the first FSW Prime Time champion at High Impact on 27 August 2000. Marc North won it from him in a three-way at Total Annihellation and vacated it at Fallen on 29 October 2000, calling it the Piece of Trash title. It changed hands often after that, through Kay Kash's win in a three-way at Defiance on 15 July 2001, and by the end of October 2001 the fed's title history marked it retired. The 2002 run put it up for grabs again at Genesis on 18 August 2002, as the Primetime Championship, and Angelo Deville won it; he kept it through every defence the surviving record holds, the last on 20 November 2002, when he also won Cassius Deamont's FSW contract.

events.note: The fed's own title history, as captured on 31 October 2001, heads the belt's table "Prime Time-Retired" (its April 2001 capture heads it "Prime Time"), and its champions page of December 2001 lists no Prime Time champion; neither page dates the retirement. The fed brought the title back at Genesis on 18 August 2002.

notes: Sources: the fed's own title history on thefsw.com, as the Wayback Machine captured it on 8 April and 31 October 2001; its 2002 Title Histories page; the show write-ups of both runs. The 2002 Title Histories page numbers Angelo Deville's reign fourteenth, after the thirteen of 2000–01, where the Genesis write-up puts the title up "for the first time".

name: FSW Lightweight Championship
epitaph: A championship of the fed's first run. Shelldog won it first in a four-way at High Impact on 27 August 2000, and Falken and D. Jaxx followed; on 13 October 2000 the fed's title history records it stripped from D. Jaxx and retired. It came back at Love Hurts on 26 February 2001, when Ron Jacobs won it in a three-way, and passed through T.Q. Smooth, who was stripped of it in March, Andy Overdose and Matt Senate to Chris Taylor on 4 May 2001. By the end of October 2001 the title history marked it retired again.

events.note: The fed's own title history, in both its April and October 2001 captures: "Ttile Retired | Stripped from D. Jaxx | 10/13/00 | Maximum Veloicty". The title was contested again from Love Hurts, 26 February 2001.

The fed's own title history, as captured on 31 October 2001, heads the belt's table "Lightweight-Retired" (its April 2001 capture heads it "Lightweight"), and its champions page of December 2001 lists no Lightweight champion; no date is given.

notes: Sources: the fed's own title history on thefsw.com, as the Wayback Machine captured it on 8 April and 31 October 2001; the Love Hurts write-up; the champions pages captured on 8 April and 28 December 2001.
